Both edge states render well. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/edge.html?state=empty** and `?state=autofail`).

**Your first visit — nothing saved yet** (`shot-38-edge-empty-firstrun.png`)
Instead of a blank page, you get the save box plus a friendly welcome — *"Save your first bookmark"* — explaining that pasting a link will auto-fill its details and let you add tags and a note. It orients you rather than leaving you staring at emptiness.

**Saving a page whose details can't be read** (`shot-39-edge-autofill-fail.png`)
If the app can't read the page (offline, private, or the site blocks it), it **doesn't invent anything and doesn't fail the save**. You still get the review card, with an honest amber note explaining it couldn't read the details, a **title suggested from the web address** (which you can rewrite), an empty description, and a "No preview available" placeholder. The link is saved either way — you just fill in what you want.

Two questions on these:

1. Does the **first-run welcome** feel right, or would you rather land straight on the empty save box with no welcome copy?
2. For the **unreadable page**, is "save it anyway with a web-address title and let me fill the rest" the behaviour you'd want — or would you rather the app **warn and pause** before saving something it couldn't read?
